messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

Here's the announcement. Bracketed items are the details I don't have — swap them in.

---

**[Service name] is moving to [new platform] in Q[N]**

We're moving [Service name] onto [new platform] next quarter. Here's what that means for you.

The short version: your account, your data, and your saved settings come with you. You don't need to re-register or rebuild anything. Sign in on [date] the way you always have, and you'll land on the new platform.

Why bother? The current setup has been straining for about two years. [Specific pain — e.g., "Exports over 50 MB time out"] and [second pain] are both symptoms of infrastructure we can't stretch further. Moving fixes those at the root rather than one ticket at a time.

**What changes**
- The web address becomes [new URL]. Old links redirect for [12 months].
- [Feature X] works differently — see [link] for the walkthrough.
- API keys stay valid, but [endpoint change / version note].

**What you need to do before [date]**
1. Update any bookmarks or scripts pointing at [old URL].
2. If you use [integration], reauthorize it after the switch.
3. Nothing else.

**The cutover**
[Service name] will be read-only from [time] on [date] to [time] on [date] — about [N] hours. We'll post live status at [status page URL].

If you have a workflow you're worried about, tell us now rather than after. Write to [email] or reply here, and we'll check it against the new platform before the cutover and tell you what we find.

— [Name], [Role]

---

**~255 words.** Two things worth flagging: I've assumed a data-and-accounts-migrate-with-you move, since that's the common case — if customers must re-register or re-enter payment details, that fact belongs in the first paragraph, not buried in the checklist. And the "why bother" paragraph only works if you fill in real pain points customers already feel. Generic reasons there ("better performance") read as corporate throat-clearing and will cost you more trust than saying nothing.

The text above has these problems. Rewrite it so none remain.
Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.

- bold_density:
- thematic_break:

Return only the rewritten text.

Three things change. The web address becomes [new URL], and old links redirect for [12 months]. [Feature X] works differently; see [link] for the walkthrough. API keys stay valid, but [endpoint change / version note].

Before [date], update any bookmarks or scripts pointing at [old URL]. If you use [integration], reauthorize it after the switch. Nothing else.

During the cutover, [Service name] will be read-only from [time] on [date] to [time] on [date], about [N] hours. We'll post live status at [status page URL].

That's about 240 words, and two things are worth flagging. I've assumed a move where data and accounts travel with the customer, since that's the common case.
